meta.title: Operation of Tray Dryer in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To dry crude drugs, plant powders, and herbal extracts at controlled temperatures to achieve the required moisture content for standardization and long-term storage.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for drying freshly collected plant materials, post-extraction marc, and powdered drugs prior to standardization tests.
procedure: Inspect the tray dryer for cleanliness; clean all trays with a dry cloth and ensure heating elements and fans are functional.
Switch ON the tray dryer and set the desired temperature using the thermostat: typical range for crude drugs is 40–60°C; heat-sensitive materials at 40°C or below.
Allow the dryer to reach and stabilize at the set temperature for at least 15–20 minutes before loading.
Spread the plant material evenly on the clean SS trays in a thin layer (not more than 2–3 cm depth) to ensure uniform drying.
Do not mix different plant materials on the same tray to avoid cross-contamination.
Place the loaded trays inside the dryer and close the door.
Record the start time, temperature setting, and material details in the logbook.
At regular intervals (every 30–60 minutes), turn and stir the material to expose all surfaces to hot air uniformly.
Periodically remove a small sample and weigh to monitor moisture loss — continue drying until constant weight is achieved.
Calculate the loss on drying (LOD): LOD (%) = [(Initial weight − Final weight) / Initial weight] × 100.
When the target LOD is achieved, remove trays from the dryer using heat-resistant gloves.
Allow the dried material to cool to room temperature in a desiccator before weighing and packing.
Pack the dried material in airtight containers, label with plant name, part, date, LOD, and batch number.
Switch OFF the tray dryer and record end time and final temperature in the logbook.
Clean trays after each batch with a dry brush and wipe with 70% ethanol.
precautions: Do not exceed the recommended temperature for heat-sensitive volatile-containing drugs (e.g., aromatic plants) — essential oils are lost above 40°C.
Never dry flammable solvents or solvent-wet extracts in a tray dryer — use a vacuum oven instead.
Ensure adequate spacing between trays for proper hot air circulation.
Use calibrated thermometers placed inside the drying chamber to verify actual vs. set temperature.
Do not open the dryer door frequently — each opening causes temperature drop and extends drying time.
Wear heat-resistant gloves when handling hot trays.
Ensure the exhaust vent of the tray dryer is not blocked.
